name: Oxytrel
description: Oxytrel is a synthetic oxytocin analogue enhanced with SNT-permeable pheromonal receptor agonists, creating a bidirectional empathic sensitivity that allows users to perceive and mirror the emotional states of nearby individuals with startling accuracy. Designed for therapeutic bonding sessions, it became a party drug within a year of release.
effects: Heightened perception of others' emotional states — near-telepathic social reading
Profound feelings of connection and belonging
Dissolution of social anxiety and interpersonal barriers
Physical warmth and tactile pleasure from proximity to others
side_effects: Emotional flooding in crowds — absorbing collective panic, grief, or rage without filter
Loss of self-boundary: difficulty distinguishing own emotions from others'
Post-dose emotional exhaustion and social withdrawal
Exploitation risk: users are highly susceptible to manipulation while dosed
Rare: users in proximity to severe emotional trauma can experience vicarious PTSD episodes
duration: 4-8 hours, patch removal does not immediately terminate effect
cultural_context: Oxytrel is the social drug of GLMZ's middle tiers — the communion drug, the party drug, the drug you take when you want to feel like the city loves you back. It's standard at Tier 2 block parties and Tier 3 corporate social events alike. The danger is well-documented and largely ignored. A subculture of 'Merge riders' deliberately dose in grief-dense locations — hospitals, memorial sites — claiming the absorbed sorrow is transcendent. They are not well.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 social event turned into a mass panic incident when a dosed crowd collectively absorbed the emotional state of a single attendee experiencing a psychotic break — someone needs to find out who that person was and why
A political operative is using Oxytrel to make a candidate's rallies feel genuinely moving — the emotional manipulation is technically legal and completely effective
A character wakes up after an Oxytrel night with the persistent emotional state of someone else — rage, grief, terror — that won't fade, and they need to find whose feelings they're carrying
